<header><div class="eyebrow">Controlled fixture · engineering walkthrough</div><h1>Keep Save unavailable while a write is pending</h1><p class="lede">The helper now disables the supplied button before calling persistence. It changes the label to <strong>Saved</strong> only after success, then restores the button after either success or failure.</p><p class="ref">One changed file: <code>editor.js:1</code> · base <code>898543da</code> → head <code>042b34bb</code></p></header>
<div class="note scope"><strong>Evidence boundary.</strong> This is controlled test data. The embedded image is an existing source-driven harness capture for this helper. No real product or Playwright suite was run for that capture or this explanation. It is not a GateReeve product screen.</div>
<h2>The behavior in one sequence</h2><p>The helper takes two inputs: a button and an asynchronous <code>persist</code> function. The supplied repository contains no caller or persistence implementation. The head commit’s stated intent is “Prevent repeated save while pending”; the code delivers a button-level interaction guard.</p>
<div class="columns"><article class="card"><span class="tag">BASE · source-grounded sequence</span><h3>The button stays available</h3><div class="path"><div class="step">User activates Save</div><div class="arrow">↓ call persist() and wait</div><div class="step">Pending: this helper never disables the button</div><div class="arrow">↓ persistence resolves</div><div class="step">Set label to Saved</div></div><p class="small">A second activation can reach the caller while the first write is pending, if the caller has no separate guard. No base-revision runtime capture is available.</p><p class="ref">Base: <code>editor.js:1</code></p></article>
<article class="card"><span class="tag">HEAD · source-grounded sequence</span><h3>The pending window is guarded</h3><div class="path"><div class="step">User activates Save → disable button</div><div class="arrow">↓ call persist() and wait</div><div class="step">Pending: button remains disabled</div><div class="arrow">↓ success sets Saved; failure skips that label</div><div class="step">Finally: re-enable button in either outcome</div></div><p class="small">Failure still rejects the returned promise. The helper adds no error message or retry policy.</p><p class="ref">Head: <code>editor.js:1</code></p></article></div>
<h2>What creates that behavior</h2><p>The disable happens synchronously before <code>persist()</code> is invoked. The <code>try</code> encloses both invocation and the wait, so <code>finally</code> restores the button when persistence resolves, rejects, or throws synchronously. It does not swallow the error.</p>
<div class="columns"><article><h3>Before</h3><pre><code>export async function save(button, persist) {
  await persist();
  button.textContent = 'Saved';
}</code></pre><p class="ref">Base <code>898543da5eb46a7ad259d241d26d502f9bb77106</code><br><code>editor.js:1</code> · reformatted for reading</p></article><article><h3>After</h3><pre><code>export async function save(button, persist) {
  button.disabled = true;
  try {
    await persist();
    button.textContent = 'Saved';
  } finally {
    button.disabled = false;
  }
}</code></pre><p class="ref">Head <code>042b34bbd87ba1f553746e2e47aa88acc9b6bdba</code><br><code>editor.js:1</code> · reformatted for reading</p></article></div>
<p>The entire scoped diff is shown above in reformatted form. No other file changed. The existing test and capture configuration provide context, but are not new coverage introduced by this change.</p>

The configured results directory was absent.</p>
<h2>Where a reviewer should look closely</h2><ul>
<li><strong>The guard is the button.</strong> <code>editor.js:1</code> does not check for an already-running call. Direct concurrent calls to <code>save()</code> still invoke <code>persist()</code> twice, and the first completion can re-enable the shared button while the other call remains pending. Whether real callers permit that is unknown because none are supplied.</li>
<li><strong>Recovery unconditionally enables.</strong> The final assignment sets <code>disabled = false</code> rather than restoring earlier state. If another rule needs to keep the same button disabled, this helper can overwrite that rule. The fixture provides no such caller, so this is a contract question, not a demonstrated product defect.</li>
<li><strong>The visible test covers only pending.</strong> Source inspection explains success and rejection paths; the harness image supports only the unresolved state. Error presentation and persistence completion remain unobserved.</li>
</ul>
